Create a fictional educational explainer for CYBERAWARE 3D about QR-code phishing. Scenario: A QR code on a meeting-room poster promises access to the conference Wi-Fi. After scanning, it opens a sign-in page on a domain unrelated to the venue. Explain why the correct defensive response is: Check the displayed URL, close the page, and ask facilities/IT for the official network instructions. Also contrast the unsafe alternatives using short abstract visual cues. Conclude with: QR codes conceal destinations; assess the actual URL before authenticating. Use a generic simulated interface, a navy/cyan 3D cyber-learning environment, legible labels, restrained camera motion, no recognizable logos, no real personal data, no operational attack instructions, no real credentials or live URLs.

VISUAL STYLE
Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

GENERATION INSTRUCTIONS
- Use the narration as the voiceover source; preserve its meaning and do not add unsupported technical claims.
- Render a 16:9 MP4 at 1080p or equivalent; keep text inside safe margins.
- Use only fictional names, domains, screens and values. Never render real secrets, OTPs, account data or real target systems.
- Provide a separate WebVTT caption file and transcript; do not rely on burned-in text alone.
- Use no flashing effects, rapid strobing, unnecessary parallax or autoplay audio.
- Human-review the rendered video for factual accuracy, spelling, pronunciation, captions and timing before marking it validated.
